name: Deeprun Tram
summary: Beneath the mountains, the Deeprun Tram carries travelers between Ironforge and Stormwind City. King Magni Bronzebeard commissioned it after the Second War, and its twin tracks carry citizens, soldiers, and goods between the Alliance capitals.

sections.title: A Marvel of Subterranean Engineering
sections.body:
After the Second War, King Magni Bronzebeard sought a faster way to send dwarven aid and supplies to Stormwind. Mountain passes made the journey slow, so he asked High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque to design an underground railway.

Gnomish engineers cut a route beneath a mountain and through a vast subterranean lake. Rats plagued the work, but the tram was finished. It carries thousands between Ironforge and Stormwind without charge.

faq.q: Why was the Deeprun Tram built?
faq.answer: After the Second War, King Magni Bronzebeard needed a faster route for supplies and dwarven troops aiding Stormwind's rebuilding and defense. He commissioned High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque to design and build the underground railway linking the two capitals.

faq.q: How does the tram travel underwater?
faq.answer: While digging between Dun Morogh and Stormwind, gnomish engineers breached a vast subterranean lake. They built a sealed, reinforced glass tunnel through the water, where passengers can watch threshadons and sharks swim beside the track.

faq.q: Why are there so many rats along the tracks?
faq.answer: The dark, damp shafts along the tracks give vermin room to breed. Gnomish station masters struggle to keep rats from chewing cables and overrunning platforms, and travelers and rat catchers like Monty sometimes help thin their numbers.

faq.q: Is the tram free to ride?
faq.answer: Yes. Ironforge and Stormwind sponsor the tram as a civic and military service. It runs continuously without fare for citizens and Alliance allies.

angles.text: The railway is a gnomish engineering achievement, with advanced track propulsion, reinforced glasswork made to withstand the depths of a subterranean lake, and intricate electrical switching stations.
For the Alliance, the tram links two of its most fortified capitals. It lets troops move quickly between them and supports their mutual defense.
